title: Non-Functional Requirements: Performance, Scalability & Capacity Design Document
summary: project-management/design/08-nfr-performance-capacity.md — concurrency/pool-sizing model, search and write cost models, and a benchmark-methodology summary that links to BENCHMARKS.md rather than copying its numbers (so it never goes stale).
description:
Write project-management/design/08-nfr-performance-capacity.md. Ground it in db/connection.py, repositories/base.py's EXACT/APPROX + hybrid RRF cost, ENH-4's consolidate_every_n, and BENCHMARKS.md's structure (not its numbers).

Required: (1) concurrency model — ConnectionPool as the hard concurrency ceiling, exhaustion behavior, sizing guidance; (2) search cost model — EXACT vs APPROX tradeoffs, the two-step ID-then-row fetch pattern's extra round-trip and why (Db2 12.1.5 fp0 constraint), hybrid=True's added Python-side RRF cost; (3) write cost model — chunking's effect on write cost, consolidate_every_n as the cost-control knob, restating ENH-4's known in-memory/no-cross-instance-sharing limitation as a capacity-planning caveat; (4) benchmark methodology summary linking to BENCHMARKS.md by relative path, with zero specific numbers copied in (so this document doesn't go stale when a new run is appended).

Fully independent of every other SDD story — new file only.
